Title: Changing a case priority retroactively erases a recorded SLA breach
Business Impact: Contractual SLA compliance reported to management and customers can be improved after the fact. A breached Critical case became "Met" (response) and "Pending" (resolution) once its priority was lowered; the dashboard response rate moved to 100 %.
User Impact: Managers cannot trust breach counts; engineers and customers see different histories for the same case.
Preconditions: Active contract with SLA targets Critical 1/2 min and Low 6000/60000 min (calendar hours); case linked to it.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create a Critical client case linked to the contract. 2. Wait until response and resolution show Breached. 3. Record a late first response. 4. As TIO Manager edit the case and set priority Low.
Expected Result: Obligations already breached stay Breached; the new target applies only to obligations still running, or the change is refused/needs an audited override.
Actual Result: Response Breached -> Met, resolution Breached -> Pending; applied target replaced by the Low target with the original start time.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc SLA-07, SLA-08); automated test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-001 in automated-tests/specs/05-known-defects.spec.ts; source src/TioHub.Api/Modules/Work/CaseSla.cs:119,228-236.
Root Cause: Confirmed: the save hook re-runs Snapshot() whenever Priority is modified on a linked case and recomputes both obligations from case creation with the new targets; no terminal-state protection.
Recommended Fix: Freeze an obligation once it is Met or Breached; on priority change keep a history of applied targets and measure each interval against the target in force; require a reason and show the override in the SLA panel.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a case whose response is Breached, when priority changes, then response status and breach time are unchanged and the timeline shows the target change; SLA report counts are unchanged.

Title: An engineer can remove the contract link from a breached case and the breach disappears from all SLA figures
Business Impact: Any user with the Edit right can take a breached case out of SLA measurement with a free-text reason. Breach count for the audit client fell from 3 to 1 after two such manipulations.
User Impact: SLA dashboard, case list filter "sla=breached" and the SLA compliance report under-report breaches.
Preconditions: Case linked to a contract, at least one obligation Breached.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Sign in as DEV\engineer. 2. POST /cases/{id}/contract with contractId null and a reason.
Expected Result: Unlinking or changing the contract of a case with a completed or breached obligation is refused, or needs the TIO Manager, and the earlier measurement is retained.
Actual Result: 204; case shows Not applicable for both obligations and is no longer counted.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc SLA-09, SLA-10 and the two "list sla=breached" counts); test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-002; src/TioHub.Api/Modules/Work/CaseEndpoints.cs:368-386.
Root Cause: Confirmed: the endpoint only calls RequireMaintain (Edit right) and has no rule on SLA state; Snapshot() with no contract clears the measurement.
Recommended Fix: Restrict contract changes after the first SLA event to holders of Manage, require a reason, keep the superseded measurement as history and report "contract changed after breach" separately.
Acceptance Criteria: An engineer receives 403/422 when unlinking a contract from a case with a Met/Breached obligation; a manager override is listed in the SLA report.

Title: First response can be back-dated to before the deadline after the breach was recorded
Business Impact: Response-time compliance depends on an unverified, user-entered timestamp; a breached response became Met by entering the case creation time.
User Impact: Reported response performance may not reflect what customers experienced.
Preconditions: Linked case whose response deadline has passed with no response recorded.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. As engineer POST /cases/{id}/first-response with respondedAt = case createdAt and any channel.
Expected Result: A response time earlier than the moment of entry needs evidence (attachment/reference) and, once the deadline has passed, approval by the TIO Manager; the entry time is shown next to the claimed time.
Actual Result: 204; status Breached -> Met; only a timeline note records it.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc SLA-06); test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-003; CaseEndpoints.cs:349-365.
Root Cause: By design the time is manual (the hub has no mail/Jira integration); there is no control for late back-dated entries.
Recommended Fix: Keep both "claimed" and "recorded at" times, flag back-dated responses in the SLA panel and report, require evidence text and manager confirmation when the claim flips a breach.
Acceptance Criteria: Back-dated entry after the deadline is refused for engineers or stored as "claimed, awaiting confirmation" and counted as breached until confirmed.

Title: Closed and cancelled cases remain editable (title, impact, priority, due date)
Business Impact: The record of a finished case can be rewritten: priority was changed High -> Low and a due date set to 2030 on a Closed case. Priority changes also re-trigger SLA evaluation (see 001). Title and impact edits do not appear in the case timeline (only in field history).
User Impact: Closed-case reports, case aging and SLA history are not stable; reviewers cannot rely on what was agreed at closure.
Preconditions: A case in status Closed or Cancelled.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Close a case through the normal workflow. 2. PUT /cases/{id} with a new title/impact/priority. 3. POST /cases/{id}/due with a new date and reason.
Expected Result: 422 "Reopen the case before changing it" (as already implemented for owner changes and progress updates).
Actual Result: 204 for all three; timeline shows PriorityChanged and DueChanged after Closed.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc CASE-31, CASE-32, CASE-33 and the printed timeline); tests TIO-DEV-AUDIT-004 (two); CaseEndpoints.cs:175-216 and 507-523.
Root Cause: Confirmed: PUT and /due have no IsOpen(status) check, unlike /assign (line 253) and /progress (line 300).
Recommended Fix: Add the open-status guard to PUT, /due, /contract, /jira and /first-response (except documented corrections by a manager with a reason).
Acceptance Criteria: All edits on Closed/Cancelled cases return 422 unless performed through an explicit, audited manager correction.

Title: A missed commitment is reported "Completed on time" after its owner moves the deadline
Business Impact: On-time delivery (KPI "on-time completion = completed by the deadline in force / completed") can be raised by the accountable owner alone: an already overdue commitment was revised to a future date with a one-word reason and then completed "on time".
User Impact: Delivery performance shown to management overstates reliability; customers experience late delivery that the hub reports as on time.
Preconditions: Open commitment past its due date, owned by an engineer.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. As the owner POST /commitments/{id}/revise with a future date and reason "moved". 2. Complete it.
Expected Result: Revising a deadline that has already passed needs approval (manager or customer reference), and the headline timeliness/KPI uses the original or last approved deadline.
Actual Result: timeliness = "Completed on time"; originalDeadlineResult = "Late" is kept but is not the reported KPI.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc COM-26, COM-27, COM-28); test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-005; src/TioHub.Api/Modules/Commitments/CommitmentEndpoints.cs:172,267; docs/DECISIONS.md A62 (KPI definition).
Root Cause: Design decision: the KPI is defined on the deadline in force and revisions need only a reason from any Edit holder.
Recommended Fix: Report both rates (vs original and vs agreed deadline); allow post-due revisions only with manager approval; show revision count in the performance report.
Acceptance Criteria: A commitment revised after its due date by its owner is not counted on time unless a manager approved the revision.

Title: No server-side protection against duplicate submissions
Business Impact: Repeated or parallel identical requests create duplicate operational records that inflate open-work KPIs. The browser button is protected against double click; scripts, retries after timeouts and multiple tabs are not.
User Impact: Duplicate cases must be found and cancelled manually.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Send the same POST /cases body three times in parallel.
Expected Result: One record; later identical requests within a short window return the first record (as exports already do, DECISIONS A62) or 409.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc CASE-11, COM-07); misc run "3 parallel identical creates -> [201, 201, 201]"; test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-006.
Root Cause: No idempotency key or duplicate rule on work records (environments, assets, installations and client aliases do have uniqueness rules).
Recommended Fix: Accept an Idempotency-Key header from the SPA or apply the 10-second identical-request rule already used for exports.
Acceptance Criteria: Three identical parallel POSTs create exactly one case.

Title: Illogical dates are accepted: due dates in the past, deadlines revised into the past, payment paid in the future
Business Impact: Records are born overdue (a case due 01 Jan 2020 appeared at the top of "Needs immediate attention" as 2,506 days overdue) and payment history can state a future paid date.
User Impact: Attention queues and overdue KPIs contain artefacts; users lose confidence in the list.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create a case or commitment with dueLocal 2020-01-01. 2. Revise a commitment to 2021. 3. Save a contract payment with status Paid and paidOn 2031-01-01.
Expected Result: Refused, or accepted only with an explicit "logged after the fact" confirmation.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc CASE-03, COM-02, COM-09, CON-09); screenshot screenshots/desktop-dashboard.png; test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-007.
Root Cause: Missing lower-bound checks on due dates and upper-bound check on PaidOn.
Recommended Fix: Validate due >= now (with an explicit override flag for retrospective logging) and paidOn <= today.
Acceptance Criteria: Past due dates return 422 unless the override flag and a reason are supplied.

Title: A completed commitment can still be edited
Business Impact: The description, type, owner and case/project links of a fulfilled commitment can be changed after completion, altering the historical delivery record.
User Impact: Completed-work history is not reliable evidence.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Complete a commitment. 2. PUT /commitments/{id} with a different description.
Expected Result: 422 (revise and cancel are already refused for completed commitments).
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc COM-23); test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-008; CommitmentEndpoints.cs:141.
Root Cause: PUT has no status guard; /revise and /cancel do.
Recommended Fix: Refuse edits unless the commitment is Open.
Acceptance Criteria: PUT on a Completed or Cancelled commitment returns 422.

Title: Missing uniqueness rules: contract reference, client name, firewall rule
Business Impact: Two Active contracts with the same contract number in one project, two clients with the same name, and identical firewall rules can coexist. Search, reports and SLA linking become ambiguous.
User Impact: Users pick the wrong contract when linking a case; duplicates accumulate.
Preconditions: Existing contract with a reference; existing client; existing rule.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. POST the same contract twice. 2. Create a client with an existing name and a new alias. 3. POST the same firewall rule twice.
Expected Result: 409 with the conflicting record named (as for client alias, environment, server and installation names).
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc CON-05, CLI-05, FW-05); test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-009.
Root Cause: No unique rule/index on Contract.ContractReference per client, Client.Name, or (source, destination, ports, protocol).
Recommended Fix: Add unique checks (and database indexes) or at least a duplicate warning such as GET /clients/duplicates already offers for clients.
Acceptance Criteria: A second contract with the same non-empty reference for the same client returns 409.

Title: Ownership is not enforced: any user with Edit can cancel, close or change any case or commitment
Business Impact: Accountability controls are weaker than the screens suggest. A second engineer cancelled a commitment owned by a colleague; the same check guards case close, cancel, waiting, due date and contract link.
User Impact: Work can be closed or cancelled by someone who is not responsible for it; only the audit trail reveals it afterwards.
Preconditions: Two engineer accounts; record owned by the first.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. As DEV\engineer2 POST /commitments/{id}/cancel on a commitment owned by DEV\engineer.
Expected Result: 403 unless the caller is owner, backup, coordinator, team lead or TIO Manager.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc COM-19, COM-29); test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-010; src/TioHub.Api/Modules/Shared/Services.cs:76-81 (RequireMaintain ignores its responsibleUserIds parameter).
Root Cause: Confirmed: after decision A22 (two roles, everyone edits everything) the method returns for any Edit holder; the owner arguments passed by 20+ call sites are dead.
Recommended Fix: Decide the intended rule. Either enforce owner/backup/coordinator/lead for state changes (cancel, close, due, contract) or remove the dead parameters and document that ownership is advisory.
Acceptance Criteria: A non-owner engineer gets 403 on cancel/close of another person's record, or the product documentation states that ownership is not an access control.

Title: The delete-with-everything endpoint needs neither record version nor server-side confirmation, and hard-deletes operational history
Business Impact: One request by a holder of Delete removed a client with 107 dependent records. The "I understand" tick is enforced only in the browser. Cases, commitments and escalations (including breached ones) can be hard-deleted and then vanish from every KPI and report.
User Impact: A mis-click or stale tab can remove a client tree; performance history can be removed rather than archived.
Preconditions: User with the Delete records right (TIO Manager by default).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. DELETE /api/v1/dependents/clients/{id} without If-Match.
Expected Result: 428/412 without the current version; a server-validated confirmation (for example the record code); work records with SLA history can only be archived.
Actual Result: 200; everything deleted in one transaction; one audit entry with counts.
Evidence: Preview GET /dependents/clients/16 returned total 107; cleanup run (client TIO_AUDIT_TEST_C1 -> 200); test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-011; src/TioHub.Api/Modules/Shared/Cascade.cs:262-284,295-296; screenshots/probe-delete-dialog.png.
Root Cause: The endpoint takes only kind and id; ExpectVersion is not called; deletes run as raw SQL that bypasses the audit save hook (one summary entry is written).
Recommended Fix: Require If-Match and a typed confirmation token validated on the server; restrict hard delete of cases/commitments/escalations to records without history, otherwise archive; keep a tombstone for KPI periods.
Acceptance Criteria: DELETE without the current version returns 428; deleting a case that has SLA results is refused with "archive instead".

Title: Escalation targets earlier than the received time are accepted
Business Impact: An escalation can be created already "30 days past response target", producing a Critical attention item on the dashboard from inconsistent input.
User Impact: Escalation attention list shows artefacts.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. POST /escalations with receivedAt = now-1h, responseDueAt = now-30d, resolutionDueAt = now-29d.
Expected Result: 422 "Targets cannot be before the escalation was received".
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc ESC-04); screenshots/desktop-dashboard.png (row "ESC-1002 ... 30 d 0 h overdue"); test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-012; src/TioHub.Api/Modules/Escalations/Escalations.cs:288-289.
Root Cause: Only "received not in future" and "resolution not before response" are checked.
Recommended Fix: Add responseDueAt >= receivedAt.
Acceptance Criteria: Request returns 422 with the field named.

Title: Invalid values produce a generic 400 with no field; some forms report one error at a time
Business Impact: Integrations and the UI cannot tell users which value is wrong when an enum or filter value is unknown.
User Impact: Users see "The request could not be read. Check the values entered and try again." without a field.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. POST /escalations with direction "ReceivedFromClient". 2. GET /cases?priority=Bogus. 3. POST /environments {} (only "Select the client." is returned).
Expected Result: 422 with errors keyed by field, all problems in one response.
Actual Result: 400 without errors; environments return a single error.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc ESC-02 first run, ENV-01); misc run "bad enum filter 400"; test TIO-DEV-AUDIT-013.
Root Cause: Enum binding fails in the JSON/query binder before validation runs; environment validation returns early.
Recommended Fix: Bind enums as nullable strings validated in Check, or map binder failures to field errors.
Acceptance Criteria: Unknown enum value returns 422 naming the field and the accepted values.

Title: Case workflow depends on the TIO Manager at triage and reopen, forces five steps for every case, and lets one person validate their own work
Business Impact: Every case must pass New -> Triaged -> In progress -> Pending validation -> Closed. Only holders of Manage can triage or reopen; an engineer who logs a Critical incident cannot start work until a manager acts. The engineer who requests validation can also close the case, so "validation" is not an independent check.
User Impact: Out of hours or during manager absence urgent work is blocked in New; simple requests cost five actions; the validation step gives false assurance.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. As engineer create a case. 2. Try triage (403) and start (422: needs Triaged). 3. After manager triage: start, request validation and close as the same engineer.
Expected Result: Engineers can triage their own team's cases (or Critical cases auto-triage); low-priority requests have a short path; the closer differs from the requester of validation or the customer confirmation is recorded.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc CASE-12, CASE-14, CASE-24, CASE-27, CASE-30); CaseEndpoints.cs:219-246,389-425,444-472.
Root Cause: Design decision A22/A61 (manager-only coordination) applied to a mandatory step.
Recommended Fix: Allow team leads/engineers to triage within their team, add a "resolve directly" path for Low/Normal requests, and record who validated (customer contact or second person).
Acceptance Criteria: An engineer can move a Critical case of their team to In progress without a manager; closure stores a validator different from the resolver or an explicit customer confirmation.

Title: SLA and completion clocks start at data entry: there is no "reported at" time and events before the record was created are refused
Business Impact: A case logged 3 hours after the customer reported it starts its SLA clock at creation, so measured response/resolution times are systematically too good. A commitment fulfilled yesterday and recorded today cannot be completed with the true time ("cannot be before the commitment was created"); a first response sent before the case was typed in is refused.
User Impact: Users must falsify times or lose the true history; SLA figures are biased in TIO's favour.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create a commitment. 2. Complete it with completedAt one minute before creation. 3. Record a first response earlier than case creation.
Expected Result: Cases carry "reported at" (default now, editable, audited) used as SLA start; completion/response times may precede record creation when justified.
Actual Result: 422 in both cases; SLA start = CreatedAt.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc COM-20 first run, COM-12); CommitmentEndpoints.cs:204; CaseEndpoints.cs:360; DECISIONS A61 ("Start = case creation").
Root Cause: Simplification in A61; the hub has no intake integration.
Recommended Fix: Add Case.ReportedAt and use it as the SLA clock start; relax the lower bound for completion and first response to the reported time.
Acceptance Criteria: A case with reportedAt 2 h ago shows a response deadline 2 h earlier than one created now.

Title: Top navigation is clipped at 1366 x 768
Business Impact: On the most common laptop resolution the first tab reads "shboard" and "Administration" is cut off under the account selector.
User Impact: Navigation labels are partly unreadable; the product looks unfinished on standard laptops.
Preconditions: Viewport 1366 x 768, TIO Manager (9 tabs), development header (account selector present).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open any page at 1366 x 768.
Expected Result: All tabs visible, or an overflow menu.
Actual Result: Tabs scroll horizontally inside the header and are covered at both ends.
Evidence: screenshots/laptop-cases.png, laptop-client-detail.png, laptop-contract-edit.png; test "@defect top navigation tabs are fully visible at 1366x768".
Root Cause: Header uses a horizontally scrolling tab strip with fixed right-hand controls; 9 sections + search + New + account do not fit. Needs verification in Forms sign-in mode, where the development account selector is absent.
Recommended Fix: Collapse sections into a "More" menu below ~1500 px or move primary navigation to the side bar; shorten the search box on small widths.
Acceptance Criteria: At 1366 px every top-level section label is fully visible or reachable from a visible overflow control.

Title: Layout overflows on phone and tablet; version matrix overflows on laptop
Business Impact: At 390 px seven pages are wider than the screen (dashboard 693 px, version matrix 1,576 px). The version matrix also overflows at 1366 and 768 px. Filters take the whole first screen on a phone and the status bar wraps to two lines.
User Impact: On-call engineers cannot use the hub comfortably from a phone or tablet.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open the listed pages at the stated width.
Expected Result: No horizontal page scroll; wide tables scroll inside their panel; filters collapse.
Actual Result: document.scrollWidth exceeds the viewport on the listed pages.
Evidence: traces/ui-crawl-results.json (fields docW, overflowX, wideEls); screenshots/mobile-dashboard.png, mobile-cases.png, mobile-versions.png, laptop-versions.png; test "@defect no horizontal page overflow at mobile".
Root Cause: Chart panels, the SLA edit table and the matrix have fixed minimum widths outside a scroll container; no mobile filter pattern.
Recommended Fix: Wrap wide tables/charts in overflow containers, collapse filters behind a "Filters" button below 900 px, hide the status bar on phones.
Acceptance Criteria: scrollWidth <= viewport width on all routes at 390, 768 and 1366 px.

Title: Accessibility: contrast, colour-only links, small targets, modal focus not contained, no focus move to errors
Business Impact: axe-core (WCAG 2.2 A/AA rules) reports 81 contrast failures on 26 of 64 screens (muted text #6b7487 on #f5f5f6 = 4.3:1 at 12 px), 55 links distinguishable by colour only on 9 screens, 19 undersized targets; 1,356 of 3,569 interactive elements (38 %) are smaller than 24 px in one dimension. Keyboard focus leaves the delete dialog while it is open, and after a failed submit focus stays on the page body.
User Impact: Users with low vision, motor impairment or keyboard-only use are disadvantaged; WCAG 2.2 AA is not met.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Run axe on each route. 2. Open a delete dialog and press Tab 12 times. 3. Submit an empty case form.
Expected Result: No serious axe violations; focus stays inside modal dialogs; focus moves to the error summary.
Actual Result: See counts above; positives: skip link, visible 2 px focus ring, labels on all 15 case-form controls, aria-invalid on failed fields, role=dialog with aria-modal.
Evidence: traces/ui-crawl-results.json (field axe, small); probe output in 12-ACCESSIBILITY-REVIEW.md; screenshots/probe-delete-dialog.png, probe-case-new-empty-submit.png.
Root Cause: Token --muted is tuned for white, not for the grey strip; row height token 26 px and 11-12 px text make targets small; Dialog component focuses the first field but has no focus trap.
Recommended Fix: Darken --muted to >= #5c6577 on grey surfaces, underline inline links, raise minimum control height to 28-32 px, add a focus trap to Dialog, focus the error summary (role=alert) after failed submits.
Acceptance Criteria: axe reports 0 serious/critical violations on all routes; Tab never leaves an open modal.
Regression Test: Add axe check to the regression suite

Title: Case list has three overlapping filter mechanisms; "Filter this page" searches only the 15 loaded rows
Business Impact: A user typing a case title into "Filter this page..." gets "no rows" for cases that exist on page 2. There are a filter bar (8 controls), a per-page text filter, a header filter row (search, client, status, priority) and two "Export CSV" buttons with different scope (all matching rows vs the page shown).
User Impact: Missed records, wrong exports, slower triage. Violates consistency and error-prevention heuristics.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open /cases. 2. Type the title of a case on page 2 into "Filter this page...".
Expected Result: One search that queries the server and one export with an explicit scope.
Actual Result: Zero rows; the header "Search title or ref" finds it.
Evidence: screenshots/desktop-cases.png; src/web/src/ui/kit.tsx:285 (placeholder "Filter this page...").
Root Cause: The generic DataTable adds client-side filter/export to tables that are already server-filtered (decision A37).
Recommended Fix: Remove the per-page filter and second export on server-paged lists; merge header filters into the filter bar; show active filters as chips.
Acceptance Criteria: Each list has one search box that searches all pages and one export button stating its row count.
Regression Test: UI test: search finds a record on page 2

Title: Create and edit forms open for users without the Edit right; refusal text is misleading
Business Impact: A read-only role can open the full "New case" form by address and only learns on submit that it is not allowed; the API message says "Your account has no role in the hub" although the account has a role.
User Impact: Wasted effort and confusing guidance for read-only stakeholders.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Sign in with a role without Edit. 2. Open /cases/new.
Expected Result: A clear "This page needs the Edit records right" page (as /admin/users does).
Evidence: screenshots/probe-role-DEV_tio_audit_test_ro-cases-new.png; traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc RO-02..RO-06); test "@defect read-only route guard"; Services.cs:80.
Root Cause: Routes are guarded only for administration; message text predates configurable roles (A31).
Recommended Fix: Guard create/edit routes by right in the router; change the message to name the missing right.
Acceptance Criteria: A user without Edit sees a refusal page on every /new and /edit route.

Title: Destructive actions are too prominent and ambiguously labelled
Business Impact: Every table row shows a red "Delete" (hard delete with dependents) as its only visible action; the case page shows nine flat buttons with "Close" (primary), "Cancel case" (red) and "Delete" side by side; the cancel dialog offers "Cancel" and "Cancel case" next to each other.
User Impact: High risk of irreversible mistakes; the common next step is hard to find among rare ones.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open /cases. 2. Open a case. 3. Press "Cancel case".
Expected Result: Primary next step first; rare and destructive actions in an overflow menu; unambiguous dialog buttons ("Keep case" / "Cancel case").
Evidence: screenshots/desktop-cases.png, desktop-case-detail.png, mobile-case-detail.png, probe-delete-dialog.png.
Root Cause: DataTable DeleteAction is rendered for every row for Delete holders (A37); action grouping (A33) not applied to cases.
Recommended Fix: Move Delete to a row/record overflow menu, prefer Archive, order case actions by workflow, rename dialog buttons.
Acceptance Criteria: No list shows a one-click Delete per row; case page shows at most three primary actions.

Title: Inconsistent typography, date formats and wording
Business Impact: 14 font sizes are in use (10, 10.5, 11, 11.4, 11.5, 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5, 14, 18, 22, 24, 28 px; 163 font-size declarations in app.css); most text is 11-12.5 px. One case page shows three date formats ("12 Nov 2026, 15:56", "2026-11-10 15:56 +04:00 (Asia/Dubai)", native "11/13/2026, 09:00 AM"). Messages expose internal names ("This step needs status PendingValidation", "the title can be at most 200 characters."), the SLA column uses unexplained "R"/"X", pager reads "Records :- 15 OF 25", pending values show "Unknown".
User Impact: Lower readability and perceived quality; users must learn several conventions.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open /cases and a case page.
Expected Result: One type scale (4-5 sizes, body >= 13-14 px), one date format with time zone on hover, sentence-case messages using labels.
Evidence: traces/ui-crawl-results.json (field fonts); screenshots/desktop-cases.png, desktop-case-detail.png; traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc CASE-06, CASE-13).
Root Cause: Sizes are set per component instead of from tokens (tokens.css defines only 5); several formatting helpers; enum names interpolated into messages.
Recommended Fix: Reduce to the token scale, centralise date formatting, map enums to labels in error text, label SLA chips "Response"/"Resolution".
Acceptance Criteria: Computed font sizes on any page come from the token set; no message contains a PascalCase enum name.
Regression Test: Lint rule on font-size; message snapshot test

Title: Error and empty states lack recovery actions
Business Impact: A failed list load shows "Something went wrong (trace ...)" with no Retry; a missing record shows a bare banner with no title, back link or search.
User Impact: Users must reload the browser or navigate manually.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Make the list request fail. 2. Open /cases/999999.
Expected Result: Retry button; not-found page with heading and links.
Evidence: screenshots/probe-api-500-case-list.png, laptop-case-missing.png.
Root Cause: StateMessage component renders text only.
Recommended Fix: Add Retry to the shared error state and a standard not-found panel for records.
Acceptance Criteria: Error state offers Retry; missing record page has an h1 and a link to the list.

Title: No VITRONIC GUI framework exists in the code base: the look is a hand-written imitation of one reference screenshot
Business Impact: The "framework" is 919 lines of bespoke CSS and a 572-line component file reproducing a VITS screenshot (colours are "visual estimates"). There is no shared, versioned, tested component library, no documentation site, no theming and no accessibility baseline to inherit; every fix must be made in this application only.
User Impact: Higher maintenance cost, visual drift from other VITRONIC products, and reference traits that limit usability (34 px bars, 24-26 px rows, 10.5-12 px text, dense flat panels).
Steps to Reproduce: Review docs/DESIGN-RULES.md, src/web/src/styles/tokens.css, app.css, ui/kit.tsx.
Expected Result: A maintained design system (tokens + accessible components) consumed as a package.
Evidence: docs/DESIGN-RULES.md ("Colours ... visual estimates"); src/web/src/styles/tokens.css:1-2; src/web/src/ui/kit.tsx; see 06-VITRONIC-GUI-FRAMEWORK-REVIEW.md.
Root Cause: Design decision: match a screenshot because no library or official assets were supplied (DECISIONS A15).
Recommended Fix: Obtain the official VITRONIC library if one exists; otherwise formalise this kit as a small design system on accessible primitives and relax the reference geometry.
Acceptance Criteria: Components come from a versioned package with documented tokens and automated accessibility tests.

Title: Operations Command Center is overloaded
Business Impact: The landing page is 5,376 px tall at 1920 px (about five screens) with roughly 60 tiles, charts and tables, eight requests and the slowest load of the application (1.8 s locally). Headline rates are shown from very small samples ("Contractual SLA met 75 %", "100 %" from 3 cases) without a sample-size warning.
User Impact: The answer to "what needs me now" competes with reference charts; percentages can mislead.
Steps to Reproduce: Open / at 1920x1080.
Expected Result: One screen of decision-relevant figures with drill-in pages per topic; rates show n and are suppressed below a minimum sample.
Evidence: screenshots/desktop-dashboard.png; traces/ui-crawl-results.json (dashboard loadMs 1806, 8 API calls).
Root Cause: Successive owner requests (A39, A50, A51, A59-A61) added bands to one page.
Recommended Fix: Keep KPI band + attention queue on the landing page; move bands to tabs/pages; show "n = 3" beside rates.
Acceptance Criteria: Landing page fits within two screens at 1920x1080; every rate displays its denominator.

Title: Test and delivery pipeline: tests run only on Windows/LocalDB, no CI, no lint, no front-end unit tests
Business Impact: The .NET tests hard-code Trusted_Connection (Windows authentication), the e2e suite requires Microsoft Edge and LocalDB, there is no CI definition, no ESLint/Prettier config and zero front-end unit tests (vitest is configured with no test files). On Linux 3 of 140 existing tests fail on file-path assumptions. 29 releases were produced in about four days without an automated gate.
User Impact: Regressions such as findings 001-013 are not caught automatically; the application cannot be verified on a build server or in containers.
Preconditions: Linux host with SQL Server container.
Steps to Reproduce: Run dotnet test with TIOHUB_TEST_SQL pointing to a SQL-auth server.
Expected Result: Tests run on any agent with a connection string; CI runs build, lint, unit, integration and e2e on every change.
Actual Result: Connection fails unless the test source is changed; result after adapting a copy: 137 passed, 3 failed.
Evidence: tests/TioHub.Tests/HubFactory.cs:21,47; tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts (channel msedge, LocalDB); traces/dotnet-existing-tests.txt; repository root has no CI or lint configuration.
Root Cause: Project built on a single Windows developer machine.
Recommended Fix: Take the full connection string from configuration, run e2e on bundled Chromium, add a CI workflow with SQL Server service container, add ESLint and component tests.
Acceptance Criteria: A clean Linux agent runs all suites green from one documented command.

Title: Four in-process background jobs and local-disk files prevent safe scale-out
Business Impact: SLA sweep, notification scan, data-quality scan and the report scheduler run as hosted services inside the web process with no leader lock; exports and attachments are on the local disk. Two instances (or IIS overlapped recycling) would run schedules twice and send duplicate notifications or reports.
User Impact: Limits availability options (no load-balanced pair) and makes recycling behaviour important.
Steps to Reproduce: Code review.
Expected Result: Jobs guarded by a database lock or run in a separate worker.
Evidence: src/TioHub.Api/Modules/ModuleRegistration.cs:35-42; Modules/Work/CaseSla.cs:306; Modules/Reporting/ReportingEndpoints.cs:314.
Root Cause: Single-server IIS deployment assumed (docs/OPERATIONS.md).
Recommended Fix: Use sp_getapplock (or a job table with leases) around each run; document single-instance constraint until then.
Acceptance Criteria: Two instances produce one scheduled export per recipient.

Title: Maintainability: very dense source, business rules inside endpoint lambdas, vestigial access model, large bundle
Business Impact: 1,116 source lines exceed 200 characters (up to 342); CaseEndpoints.cs holds 60 KB of validation and workflow logic in route lambdas; the scope/grant model (client, project, team scopes) is still stored and returned by the admin API but ignored at run time; 115 IgnoreQueryFilters calls; 41 migrations in four days; the SPA ships a single 789 KB script (224 KB gzip) plus a 757 KB map atlas.
User Impact: Slower onboarding and review, higher defect rate when rules change (see 004, 008: guards present on some endpoints and missing on siblings).
Steps to Reproduce: Static review.
Expected Result: Domain services with unit tests per rule; line length and complexity limits; route-level code splitting.
Evidence: src/TioHub.Api/Modules/Work/CaseEndpoints.cs; Modules/Shared/Services.cs:76-81; Security/SignIn.cs (AccessCalculator); src/web build output (index-*.js 788.62 kB).
Root Cause: Rapid feature delivery without refactoring.
Recommended Fix: Extract a CaseWorkflow/CommitmentWorkflow domain layer with a transition table; remove unused scope data or re-enable it; split the bundle per route.
Acceptance Criteria: Workflow rules are covered by unit tests independent of HTTP; initial script < 300 KB.

Title: Security observations: API description readable without hub access, extension-only file checks, public map tiles, no MFA
Business Impact: The OpenAPI document (318 KB, every endpoint and schema) is returned to an authenticated account that has no hub access. Attachments are accepted by extension only (a file starting "MZ" named .pdf was stored). Map tiles are fetched by users' browsers from tile.openstreetmap.org, disclosing user IP addresses and viewed regions to a third party. Forms sign-in (the production default) has no MFA; it was not testable in this build.
User Impact: Information disclosure of the API surface; malware could be stored under a harmless extension (downloads are forced as attachments with nosniff, which limits impact).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. GET /openapi/v1.json as an account that gets 403 on /api/v1/me. 2. Upload fake.pdf.
Expected Result: OpenAPI only for hub users or disabled outside development; content-type sniffing or AV scan; internal tile source.
Evidence: security run "openapi for unknown user 200 317839"; misc run "upload TIO_AUDIT_TEST_fake.pdf 200"; src/TioHub.Api/Program.cs (MapOpenApi; AppOptions.MapTileUrl); DECISIONS A18, A20.
Root Cause: MapOpenApi sits under the fallback authentication policy but outside UserContextMiddleware's /api path check.
Recommended Fix: Serve OpenAPI under /api or only in Development; add magic-number validation; configure an internal tile server; plan MFA/SSO before production.
Acceptance Criteria: Unmapped account gets 403 for /openapi/v1.json.

Title: Functional gaps against Technology Implementation & Operations practice
Business Impact: The hub has no change-management record, no problem record (root cause / known error), no shift-handover log, no knowledge base, no implementation plan with milestones-dependencies-go-live readiness-hypercare (only contract delivery-schedule rows and a "project phase" label), no risk register, no monitoring or ticket integration and no e-mail or chat notification. Environment health is entered manually.
User Impact: TIO still needs Jira, spreadsheets and e-mail beside the hub; the hub cannot yet be the single operational view it aims to be.
Steps to Reproduce: Inventory in 02-APPLICATION-INVENTORY.md.
Expected Result: See 07-TIO-OPERATIONS-ASSESSMENT.md.
Evidence: docs/openapi-v1.json (194 paths, none for changes/problems/milestones); README ("The hub never calls Jira, vaults, client systems or messaging").
Root Cause: Scope decision (BRD MVP).
Recommended Fix: Prioritise: outbound notifications, change calendar, go-live checklist/milestones, problem records linked to cases.
Acceptance Criteria: Roadmap agreed with owners.

Title: Linked cases are often "Not measurable": priorities without a target and support hours kept only as free text
Business Impact: A Normal-priority case on a contract with targets for other priorities is Not measurable and silently excluded from compliance rates; seeded contracts keep support hours in "Support notes" (for example "Mon-Fri 07:30-15:30") while the structured days and times are empty. Public holidays are not modelled.
User Impact: Compliance percentages cover an unknown share of cases.
Preconditions: Contract without a target for a priority.
Steps to Reproduce: Create a Normal case on the audit contract.
Expected Result: Data-quality rule "active contract without target for a priority / without support calendar"; coverage ratio shown beside every SLA rate.
Evidence: SLA run output (case D: NotMeasurable, applied (Normal, None, None)); screenshots/laptop-contract-edit.png; DECISIONS A61.
Root Cause: Targets are optional per priority; migration left legacy text.
Recommended Fix: Add the data-quality rule and a holiday calendar; show measured/total on SLA tiles.
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard shows "measured n of m linked cases".

Title: Reopened case keeps the previous outcome and evidence; reopen rights differ between cases and commitments
Business Impact: After reopening, the case page still shows the earlier outcome and validation evidence as current values; engineers may reopen completed commitments but only managers may reopen cases.
User Impact: An open case appears to have an outcome; inconsistent authority model.
Steps to Reproduce: Reopen as manager and read the case.
Expected Result: Outcome/evidence of the earlier cycle shown as history only; one rule for reopening.
Actual Result: outcome "done" and evidence still returned on the Triaged case; commitment reopen 204 for engineer.
Evidence: traces/api-test-evidence.jsonl (tc CASE-36 and following print, COM-25).
Root Cause: Reopen clears ClosedAt only (CaseEndpoints.cs:466-468).
Recommended Fix: Move closure fields to the cycle history on reopen; align reopen rights.
Acceptance Criteria: Reopened case returns empty outcome and lists the earlier one under history.

Title: API silently ignores unknown or invalid query parameters
Business Impact: Unknown filters (recordType/recordId on the audit list), sort=bogus and page=-1 return unfiltered data with 200, so a caller can believe a filter was applied; report endpoints, by contrast, reject unknown filters.
User Impact: Integrations and deep links can show wrong data without warning.
Steps to Reproduce: GET /admin/audit?recordType=Case&recordId=21 (returns all 652 entries).
Expected Result: 400/422 for unknown parameters.
Evidence: audit-trail run (total 652); misc run (bad sort 200, page -1 200).
Root Cause: Minimal-API binding ignores extra query keys.
Recommended Fix: Validate query keys centrally as the report registry does.
Acceptance Criteria: Unknown parameter returns 422.

Title: Users cannot be removed and a role stays locked by deactivated users
Business Impact: Accounts created by mistake can only be deactivated; a role held only by deactivated users cannot be deleted. Three synthetic audit users and two roles therefore remain in the audit database.
User Impact: Administration lists accumulate dead entries.
Steps to Reproduce: Deactivate a user, then delete its role.
Expected Result: Delete unused accounts without history, or allow role deletion when only deactivated users hold it.
Evidence: cleanup run output.
Root Cause: No delete endpoint for users.
Recommended Fix: Add user deletion for accounts with no activity; let role deletion reassign deactivated users.
Acceptance Criteria: Role with only deactivated holders can be deleted.
